caption_draft: Sentinel-2 surface-reflectance RGB composites of the 20 × 20 km Sutlej window in the dry and wet observation periods. Common UTM extent; white denotes invalid RGB data.
Wet-season Sentinel-1/2 candidate-water agreement (A) and shares of jointly valid 20 m cells (B). Agreement is not independent classification accuracy.
Optical dry-to-wet water transitions and areas also classified as wet-season SAR water. Concurrence supports a candidate-inundation interpretation; neither map confirms flood origin.

Confusion counts and class-wise sample agreement relative to purposively balanced, Sentinel-2 RGB-interpreted labels. The labels are not ground observations and do not support design-based area-adjusted accuracy.
Fitted Gaussian mixture in wet VV dB and lower-backscatter component posterior. Posterior ambiguity is model-based, not a calibrated probability of flooding.
Sensitivity of approximate inter-method agreement intervals to 0.5, 1 and 2 km spatial bootstrap blocks. Intervals quantify agreement uncertainty, not ground-truth accuracy.
Local percentage of mutually valid cells classified differently by SAR and NDFI in 1 × 1 km grid cells. Disagreement is not synonymous with error.
Change in candidate newly appearing optical water and SAR-corroborated area under stricter NDFI decision margins. Area sensitivity does not measure accuracy.
Ten-metre candidate-water intersection over union between SAR parameter variants and the prespecified baseline; stability relative to baseline is not accuracy.
